key_facts: Chest X-rays are typically the first-line imaging study for many acute and chronic thoracic complaints.
The image usually includes the lung fields, cardiac silhouette, mediastinum, diaphragm, bony thorax, and upper abdominal soft tissues.
Common views are frontal (PA or AP) and sometimes lateral.
Image quality is assessed by lung inflation, rotation, exposure, and patient positioning.
